scope: Independent challenge review of mixed-experience navigation, search, comparison and builder UX. Audit and roadmap only; preserve existing URLs and v1 system descriptions.

method.browser: CUA in-app browser, desktop default viewport, production build
evidence_types: Independent rendered DOM and UI interactions
Keyboard Enter and Tab with read-only active-element inspection
Reviewer assessment of proportionality, explicitly separated from reproductions
method.changes: Only disposable audit-origin browser inputs. No repository edits, analyzer installations or analyzer/example executions. Report is outside the repository.
method.checks_policy: The packet reports passing build and unit checks. They were not rerun here and do not establish the absence of the independently reproduced UI problems.

summary.priority_change: EXP-03: recommend P3 rather than P2. The action mismatch is now independently clicked and confirmed, but conditional classification and visible warning remain correct and a profile link is available.
important_qualifications: N01 is a concrete comparison-summary gap, not evidence that the underlying profiles lack result explanations or violate the optional decision-summary schema.
SEA-03 should guarantee taxonomy recall and reviewed positive capability terms; exact category-equivalent result sets require an explicit search-design decision.
SEA-05 establishes different global-navigation and local-filter behavior, not that preserving filters in every sidebar navigation is necessarily the correct convention.
No P1 finding is supported by this lane. Transient shortlist loss is recoverable through the earlier catalog URL and is not saved-system data loss.

reviews.verification: Independent live Static/C++ round trips through a profile and a comparison; source corroboration. Dynamic category population also checked, but its return path was not repeated live.
evidence: Static analysis with Language C++ showed 15 of 63 entries at /ToolWiki/static/?language=C%2B%2B.
Read notes on CBMC navigated to /ToolWiki/tools/cbmc/?catalog=language%3DC%252B%252B. Return to filtered results led to /ToolWiki/?language=C%2B%2B and 24 of 89 entries.
Static/C++ with CBMC and Clang Static Analyzer selected opened comparison. Direct return retained both selections but returned to the root catalog and 24 of 89 entries.
src/lib/comparison.mjs:14 excludes category from CATALOG_FILTERS; catalogHref returns the root catalog. ToolCatalog.astro:108 derives context from the form, which does not contain pathname category.
notes: This is loss of category context. Do not attribute shortlist loss to this finding: comparison return kept the shortlist, while profile shortlist loss is independently CMP-01.
P2 is proportional because the supplied explicit return action silently changes the candidate set.
acceptance_corrections: Remove duplicate acceptance bullets and replace the broad impact wording 'loses selection context' with 'loses category context'.
Preserve allowlisted category, filters, query, sort and normalized selected IDs across both profile and comparison routes; verify All, Static and Dynamic separately.
Keep legacy links valid, default invalid categories safely, and do not accept a destination URL as category context.

reviews.verification: Independent live direct-profile and comparison-profile reproductions, plus positive direct-comparison return control.
evidence: At /ToolWiki/?language=Python&compare=tools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fmypy, the UI displayed two selected tools.
Read notes on Ruff omitted selected IDs from its catalog context. Returning from the profile produced /ToolWiki/?language=Python, with both Ruff and mypy unchecked and no selection tray.
Reselected Ruff and mypy, opened Compare 2 tools, followed the Ruff table-header link, then used Return to filtered results: both checkboxes were again false.
Positive control: catalog -> Compare 2 tools -> Return to filtered results retained compare=tools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fmypy and both checkbox properties were true.

ArticleContent.astro:66 calls catalogHref(base, [], context). ToolComparison.astro:58-62 passes sanitized filter context to profile links while its direct browse link at line 132 receives selected IDs.
notes: This reproduces on All/Python, independently of ARC-01.
Recoverable transient selection loss warrants P2; it is not permanent data loss and is separate from the builder's documented temporary shortlist semantics.
acceptance_corrections: Cover catalog -> profile -> return and catalog -> comparison -> profile -> return, including zero, one, two and three valid selected IDs.
Retain the passing direct comparison-return behavior and normalize unknown, duplicate or excessive IDs.
Coordinate category context with ARC-01 without introducing arbitrary redirects or changing v1 descriptions.

reviews.verification: Independent live shortcut and proposed broader-filter check; internal catalog scope only.
evidence: Clicked Test an API from the homepage. Its q=API+testing destination returned RESTler, Schemathesis and Burp Suite Community Edition: 3 of 89.
Changed the query to HTTP and selected Running applications. Results were Burp Suite Community Edition, Burp Suite Professional, RESTler, Schemathesis and ZAP: 5 of 89.
ToolCatalog.astro:29 hardcodes the free-text API testing shortcut; this is not a maintained task-membership set.
notes: The current result set is incomplete for the broad visible task label, rather than a broken keyword-search implementation.
A narrower explicitly labeled generated/schema-testing preset could also be defensible, but the present inclusion of the manual Community edition does not express that narrower scope.
No current external API-testing capabilities were reverified by this reviewer.
acceptance_corrections: Test the membership of the broad preset against the real catalog, without relying on result order or permanently hardcoding the count five.
Keep manual testing, automated security scanning and schema-generated tests distinguishable; do not imply equivalent checks or include arbitrary protocol tools merely because they use TCP.
Keep existing bookmark queries valid.

reviews.verification: Independent keyboard reproduction on catalog and builder, with active-element and next-Tab checks.
evidence: Catalog /ToolWiki/?q=Ruff: checked Compare Ruff, then keyboard-activated Remove Ruff with Enter. document.activeElement was BODY. The next Tab focused the Skip to content anchor.
Builder existing Audit Python backend: checked only Compare Ruff, activated Remove Ruff with Enter. document.activeElement was BODY; the next Tab again focused Skip to content.
The builder's empty comparison region remained visible, but no stable focus target received focus.
ToolCatalog.astro:147 focuses a status inside the tray that was just hidden. system-builder-ui.mjs:407 tries a remaining tray button/link, which does not exist at zero selections.
notes: The defect is directly observable focus loss, not a claim about screen-reader speech or formal WCAG conformance.
P2 is appropriate for loss of place during a routine keyboard task on two primary surfaces.
acceptance_corrections: Keep an intentional visible target near the current results focused after final removal, and ensure the next Tab continues locally.
Also check removal from two or three choices and a selected tool hidden by current filters; those variants were not independently rerun in this review.
A concise announcement should accompany removal, but it does not replace the focus correction.

reviews.verification: Actual known-host answer buttons independently clicked for Binwalk and cwe-checker. Genuine unknown-host control tested with Binwalk; both candidate messages observed in that state.
evidence: Existing Audit Windows native component had C++, Native executable, Windows target and Windows analysis host. Both Binwalk and cwe-checker were Needs more information and displayed Verify analysis host OS: Windows is not in this workflow's documented examples.

Clicked each tool's Answer for Audit Windows native button. Both actions opened the component environment fields and focused a SELECT whose value remained Windows; neither opened compatibility evidence.
Set the disposable component to Binaries only, rebuild No, instrumentation No, workload Yes. The same known-Windows verification message remained.

Changed analysis host to Not sure / not specified. After the debounced update, both candidates displayed Specify analysis host OS. Clicking Binwalk's action focused the empty host SELECT, which is appropriate.
system-builder.mjs:69-74 stores missing and unlisted choices as field/message questions. system-builder-ui.mjs:104-106 always routes Answer to focusAnswer.
notes: The reported UI action mismatch is now reproduced, strengthening the original source-only click inference.

Downgrade to P3: existing uncertainty, conditional status, profile links and host explanation are accurate. The action is unhelpful for a known constraint but does not produce a false verified match or block profile access.
Changing to Linux is legitimate only if that is the intended analysis host, such as an actual Linux container. It must not be presented as a checkbox workaround for Windows compatibility.
Deduplicate MAT-02 under this finding.
acceptance_corrections: Add a distinct compatibility-evidence action for a known host outside documented examples while retaining a field action for an unknown host.
Do not promise that following a link resolves uncertainty; retain conditional status until the reviewed workflow supports the actual intended environment.
Keep explicit exclusions blocked, preserve v1 fields, and avoid a manual override that invents support.
Remove duplicate acceptance bullets in the packet.

reviews.verification: Independent live catalog queries and Pagefind comparison, with mode-population and source checks.
evidence: dynamic analysis returned only capa and FLOSS: 2 of 89. The Dynamic category itself displayed 28 of 28.
static analysis returned 29 of 89, while the Static category displayed 63 of 63.
null pointer returned 0 of 89 with no other filters. Search all pages for the same text returned four pages: clang-tidy, Infer (Pulse), cwe-checker and Cppcheck (Open Source).

The full-page snippets included explicit null-pointer-dereference/use text for cwe-checker and Cppcheck. The clang-tidy result was a null pointer constant example, illustrating that all Pagefind matches are not equivalent capability evidence.
catalog.mjs:33-34 indexes raw mode names and selected positive metadata rather than the displayed Static analysis/Dynamic analysis label phrases or full profile bodies.
notes: The vocabulary mismatch is concrete. It should not be reframed as proof that catalog coverage or the analyzers themselves are absent.
Retain P2 because the site's own taxonomy and an ordinary documented defect phrase fail expected discovery across substantial existing content.

The packet's exact corresponding-population acceptance wording is too strong for a general AND-term search unless category-intent interpretation is deliberately added. Positive lexical matches outside a mode may remain legitimate.
acceptance_corrections: Require all tools tagged with the queried taxonomy mode to be discoverable before other filters. Require exact equality only if explicit category-query semantics are chosen and documented.
Add null-pointer vocabulary only to reviewed positive capability claims; distinguish pointer-style modernization from dereference detection when presenting results.
Continue excluding caveats, unsupported capabilities and other-edition claims from capability indexing.
Retain existing title/alias and short-language checks; their full 132-query sweep was not rerun by this reviewer.

reviews.verification: All three named common-comparison result rows inspected live; source and mypy profile prose corroborated.
evidence: Ruff/mypy: What it can tell you showed diagnostics with rule code and location for Ruff, but only Type errors for mypy.
CodeQL/SpotBugs: CodeQL described alerts, locations, path-query routes and SARIF; SpotBugs showed Logic errors, Concurrency issues, Injection risks.
RTAMT/PSY-TaLiRo: RTAMT described robustness sign and margin on a supplied trace; PSY-TaLiRo showed Temporal requirement violations.
ToolComparison.astro:74 uses tool.decision.result or falls back to tool.findings. The mypy profile already has an illustrative diagnostic and interpretation at lines 63-86.
notes: This is a bounded reuse and summary-consistency gap in a decision row. It is not missing all result guidance, a regression, or a schema violation.
Keep P2 as useful next content work for the common comparisons, behind the confirmed workflow defects. Do not expand it into a mandatory rewrite of all 89 profiles based only on missing fields.
The novice audit reported successful journeys and no functional defect; those positives remain compatible with this recommendation.
acceptance_corrections: Require concrete output form, useful fields and interpretation for the three named entries, using shared reviewed content in profiles and comparisons.
Do not require the entire optional decision object solely to populate one result row unless that is an intentional schema design; avoid forcing unrelated first-try rewrites into this bounded task.
Preserve illustrative/executed labeling and avoid claims of measured coverage or comprehensive detection. Deduplicate CMP-04 here.

reviews.verification: Independent live zero-result recovery inspection and successful header full-page search.
evidence: For null pointer, the catalog empty state offered fewer terms, a starting-collection disclaimer and Reset search. It did not offer a local full-page search action.
The persistent header Search all pages was available and returned four pages after manually retyping the query.
notes: P3 is proportional. Recovery exists today; the proposed action reduces distance and retyping rather than unblocking search.
Keep the distinction between metadata search and all-page search visible. Do not silently merge their results or relax filters.
acceptance_corrections: Prefer handing the query to the existing search dialog while retaining catalog state; no third search service is warranted.
Verify keyboard focus when opening and closing the search dialog and retain the original catalog query/filters.
Keep category-broadening Search all tools separate from Search all pages.

reviews.verification: Independent live comparison of link destinations and sidebar activation.
evidence: Configured q=python type checker, input=Source code, cost=Free and sort=za: 2 of 89 entries.
The Analysis category Static analysis link carried all four fields. The Main navigation Static analysis link was /ToolWiki/static/.
Clicked the sidebar link: URL became /ToolWiki/static/ and the catalog displayed 63 of 63 entries.
notes: The behavior difference is real, but a global navigation link entering a fresh category is a reasonable convention. The current in-page filter navigation also has a reasonable continuity convention.
Do not present the proposed sidebar synchronization as an established functional requirement or imply user testing proved confusion.
P3 only; lower priority than explicit Return to filtered results losing context.
acceptance_corrections: Make the intended global-versus-local navigation convention explicit before mandating identical URLs. Either preserve supported catalog context or clearly distinguish a fresh-category entry action.
If synchronization is selected, limit it to catalog pages and use the same safe allowlisted context as local tabs; retain a clear reset path.
Existing category URLs and noncatalog navigation must remain valid.

reviews.verification: Independent live Source code/Python CodeQL card inspection, plus general rendering-source check.
evidence: After Check source code -> Python, CodeQL was a valid result but its visible Languages line was C, C++, C#, Go +9.
ToolCatalog.astro:70 always renders tool.languages.slice(0, 4) plus the hidden count, regardless of the active language.
notes: A useful confirmation cue for newcomers, but there is no incorrect match or capability claim. P3 is appropriate.
A short Matches Python cue may be clearer than reordering stable metadata, and either is a reasonable implementation choice.
acceptance_corrections: When a language filter is active, visibly identify that matched language without implying universal language/version support.
Keep result membership, existing source-input semantics and unfiltered language order stable.
Do not require every one of the original report's multilingual cards to be independently verified before accepting this shared-renderer opportunity; only CodeQL was rerun live here.

reviews.verification: Independent source inspection of the complete Trivy example, interpretation and source-link sections; no new live Trivy walkthrough.
evidence: Trivy frontmatter advertises Container images and describes supported image preparation.
The Example workflows section shows only trivy fs --scanners vuln . and trivy config .; the body explains image/repository distinctions but provides no image invocation.
The listed sources include installation, vulnerability scanner, language coverage, misconfiguration, SBOM and license links, rather than a direct image-target setup guide.
notes: This is a narrow first-step omission for a prominently advertised input, not proof that every supported target requires a local tutorial or that the two existing examples are wrong.
A precise official image-target guide adjacent to the image discussion is sufficient; a maintained runnable fixture is not required by this P3 item.
acceptance_corrections: Provide either one clearly illustrative image-specific command with target/access assumptions or a direct maintained image-target guide.
Retain package/advisory versus exploitability limits, scanner selection and execution-status labels.
Do not merge a new container fixture, analyzer installation or executed-validation project into this small change.

reviews.verification: Independent live mypy/Pyright and Trivy/OSV-Scanner comparisons plus authored-choice and existing-profile source review.
evidence: Selected mypy/Pyright in the comparison form: no How these tools relate region rendered.
Selected Trivy/OSV-Scanner: no relationship region rendered.
Ruff/mypy positive control did render the explanation that linting and type checking work together.
tool-choices.ts has seven authored pairs but not these two. Existing profile bodies explicitly link both comparisons.
notes: A targeted continuation of an existing mechanism is proportional. Missing relationship records do not invalidate the comparison table or justify a complete pairwise matrix.
The useful decision criteria require content review; the seven-record count alone is not a defect metric.
acceptance_corrections: Scope new authored guidance to these deliberately linked pairs and maintain one source of content.
Explain shared tasks, meaningful preparation differences and limits without universal rankings, raw issue-count comparisons or unverified superiority claims.
Verify new comparative capability claims against primary sources before implementation; this reviewer did not perform that external verification.

evidence: The primary Cost row displayed Free with limits, Paid in each column and contained zero links.
Show technical details and sources was initially closed. Opening it revealed the Cost and edition limits row, detailed eligibility text and See edition details links.
ToolComparison.astro:108-109 creates the edition link only for costNote, which is in detailRows.

acceptance_corrections: Expose keyboard-accessible cost/eligibility links from the primary row while retaining detailed notes and their existing scope.
Preserve Free, Free with limits and Paid distinctions; do not invent entitlement or price claims.
If implemented with profile links, include the same restored catalog/selection context addressed by CMP-01.

limitations: Agent walkthrough and design review, not a human participant study, benchmark or exhaustive accessibility audit.
No screen-reader speech testing, mobile/touch testing, true browser zoom testing or full cross-browser matrix.
No analyzer examples executed or analyzers installed. No external upstream claims newly verified.
No v1 migration, import/export, quota or large-storage edge testing; those belong to other review lanes.
Builder results are debounced. Immediate stale snapshots were followed by settled observations and were not reported as defects.
Only Static category return was reproduced live; the shared-source explanation supports Dynamic but does not substitute for a future Dynamic regression test.
The report records acceptance improvements, not product changes.
